title: fix(dedicated-autoscaler): correct burst tokenbucket refill + throughput guarantee reporting
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: we observed a production regression where dedicated fleet burst consumption could briefly exceed configured throughput guarantees under high-concurrency storms. Root cause: tokenbucket refill logic allowed fractional refills to accumulate across ticks in a way that briefly overshot the burst capacity when multiple refill events were applied concurrently; additionally utilization metrics reported to the console and billing pipeline were computed from the pre-correction in-memory counters, leading to under-reported burst utilization in dashboards. This PR fixes the tokenbucket refill race/overflow, enforces throughput guarantee checks at admission time, and harmonizes utilization reporting so dashboards and billing reflect the enforced throughput.

Changes in this PR (summary): - Fix tokenbucket concurrency and cap behavior in services/dedicated-autoscaler/tokenbucket.go so refills can't push available tokens > capacity. - Add admission-time throughput guarantee enforcement in services/dedicated-autoscaler/autoscaler.go (reject or queue requests when a guarantee would be violated). - Emit new metrics (dedicated_burst_tokens_available, dedicated_throughput_enforced, dedicated_burst_denied) and backfill reporting pipeline in observability/metrics/dedicated_metrics.go. - Add DB migration to persist burst event counters for durable reporting: db/migrations/20241110_add_burst_metrics.sql. - Add e2e test that simulates concurrency storms and asserts no guarantee violations: tests/e2e/dedicated_autoscaler_burst_test.go. - Update docs release notes and add a short troubleshooting note for operators.

Why this approach: making the throughput guarantee enforced at admission-time prevents brief oversubscription that downstream capacity accounting and billing cannot easily reconcile. Fixing the tokenbucket cap/race reduces transient overshoot windows. Emitting consistent metrics and persisting counters ensures utilization dashboards match what the autoscaler actually enforces.

Testing: added unit tests for tokenbucket edge cases, integration test for autoscaler admission logic, and an e2e that emulates a 500 concurrent short-lived request burst. CI ran whole suite; one flaky integration test was re-run and passed.

Checklist: - [x] Reproduced regression locally with stress runner - [x] Added unit & integration tests - [x] Added e2e verification - [x] Metrics emitted and dashboards updated - [x] Migration SQL included - [x] Docs/release notes updated

Related: ENG-4521 (root cause & runbook), SUP-238 (customer report).

a8d2b5f: autoscaler: check throughput guarantees at admission time; return queued response when necessary
f1a2b3c: tests: add e2e dedicated autoscaler burst scenario
9d8e7f6: db: add migration to persist burst counters
diff_snippets:
--- a/services/dedicated-autoscaler/tokenbucket.go
+++ b/services/dedicated-autoscaler/tokenbucket.go
@@
-    tb.tokens += refill
+    // ensure we never exceed configured capacity even if multiple refills race
+    tb.tokens += refill
+    if tb.tokens > tb.capacity {
+        tb.tokens = tb.capacity
+    }

release_notes: Fixes an autoscaler regression where dedicated fleet burst consumption could briefly exceed throughput guarantees under high-concurrency bursts. Adds admission-time enforcement, corrects tokenbucket refill logic, improves utilization reporting metrics, and includes a DB migration for durable burst counters. Operators: update running fleets with the 2024-11-12 release to ensure billing and dashboards reflect enforced throughput.
notes_for_ops: Run db/migrations/20241110_add_burst_metrics.sql before deploying the autoscaler change to avoid a short window where counters are not persisted. Dashboards updated in Grafana dashboard id=dedicated-fleet-utilization (refresh required).
incident_reference: Related to ENG-4521 runbook; this PR implements the long-term fix after the mitigation deployed during the incident.
